names.official: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

summary: Sri Lanka requires almost all visitors to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) — USD 50 for a 30-day double-entry tourist visit (USD 20 for South Asian nationals), or USD 60 (USD 25) when obtained on arrival — while a free tourist-ETA list of 40 countries, including India, China and Russia, has made the ETA free for many travelers.

fee.notes: USD 60 is the fee for extending to day 90 for most nationalities. The Department of Immigration and Emigration's extension fee chart runs in three bands counted from arrival — days 31–90, 91–180 and 181–270 — at USD 60, 150 and 200 for most nationalities; USD 100, 150 and 200 for the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, Norway and most EU states; and free, then USD 150 and 200, for Singapore, the Maldives, Seychelles and the Czech Republic. The United States has its own rates (USD 100 and USD 200). Apply online at eservices.immigration.gov.lk after arriving in Sri Lanka.

source.name: Department of Immigration and Emigration of Sri Lanka — Visa Fees: tourist visa extension fee chart (days 31–90, 91–180, 181–270)

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival.

source.name: Online Visa Application
U.S. Department of State — Sri Lanka country information

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required from travelers aged 9 months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including after more than 12 hours' transit through an airport in one.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read makes travel insurance a condition of entry. The UK government advises insurance for local treatment and medical evacuation: emergency treatment outside the main cities is not readily available, private hospitals can be expensive, and repatriation options in an emergency are limited.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Sri Lanka, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
The Government of Canada says exporting antiques without a proper licence is illegal.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says violent crimes against foreigners are rare but low-level opportunistic crime has increased, and that protests can happen anywhere on the island at short notice and can become violent. The Government of Canada advises a high degree of caution because of demonstrations, the threat of terrorist attacks and crime.

bestTimeToVisit.text: According to the Government of Canada, the monsoon brings rain from December to February in the northeast and from May to September in the southwest, so the two coasts are wet at different times of year. Between them come two inter-monsoon seasons, March–April and October–November, with scattered but intense rainfall and thunderstorms.

The UK Foreign Office warns that disrespecting Buddhist images and artefacts is a serious offence that can lead to arrest, that visible tattoos of Buddha can get you refused entry or deported, and that you should not pose for photographs standing in front of a statue of Buddha.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Sri Lanka?
faq.answer: Yes — an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), applied for at eta.gov.lk. Since 25 May 2026 US citizens are among the 40 nationalities that get the tourist ETA free of charge; it allows 30 days with double entry.

faq.question: Which nationalities get Sri Lanka's ETA free of charge?
faq.answer: Since 25 May 2026 the tourist ETA has been free for nationals of 40 countries, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, much of Western Europe, the Gulf states, India, China, Russia and Japan, and for Maldives, Seychelles and Singapore under reciprocal agreements. An ETA application is still required.

faq.question: Can I extend my 30-day stay in Sri Lanka?
faq.answer: Yes. The Department of Immigration and Emigration extends tourist visas online after you arrive, in bands counted from your arrival date: to day 90, to day 180 and to day 270. Fees depend on nationality — USD 60 to reach day 90 for most passports, USD 100 for the UK, US, Canada, Australia and most of Western Europe.

faq.question: How long does the Sri Lanka ETA take?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states how long an online ETA application takes. Sri Lanka's overseas missions issue an ETA or short-stay visa within 3 business days, and the ETA portal advises keeping a copy of the ETA approval to produce at the port of entry.

faq.question: What documents does Sri Lanka require on arrival?
faq.answer: A passport valid for 6 months, the ETA approval, a confirmed onward or return ticket, and proof of sufficient funds for your stay. Canada's travel advice adds that you must also fill out an online arrival card, which you can complete 3 days before arriving.
